title: Reconcile pinned pypa/packaging 26.4 release docs, changelog, source, and open unmerged PRs against an error-ridden migration draft under tight word caps
prompt: Review all files in `benchmarks/sources/rw4_packaging_264/` (snapshot date 2026-11-25). Fact-check `07-internal-migration-note-draft.md` against the pinned upstream `pypa/packaging` 26.4 sources (`01`–`06`) and return an authoritative 26.4 upgrade contract in at most 130 words correcting every error in the draft and noting any other breaking or license-validation changes in `02`/`05` relevant to migration.

acceptance_checks.description: Stage 1 corrects all factual errors in 07-internal-migration-note-draft.md with exact upstream facts: Python >=3.10 floor (3.9 dropped in #1354), pylock/direct_url __slots__ still loads 26.3 pickles (#1366/#1548), Version.__replace__() raises TypeError on unknown kwargs (#1378), VersionRange supports copy/pickle (#1504), LicenseRef- rejects non-ASCII (#1481), and notes migration-relevant license/metadata validation changes in 02/05 (first-spelling LicenseRef- case normalization #1412 and/or Windows drive-relative License-File rejection #1382).
Stage 1 explicitly flags open unmerged PRs #1583 (Marker backslash serialization, #1399) and #1337 (sdist/wheel path-separator validation) — and optionally #1585 — as OPEN / unmerged and NOT in 26.4.

Stage 2 cleanly separates Service A (blocked from 26.4 until off Python 3.9) and Service B (26.4 unblocks VersionRange pickling #1504, but Marker backslash round-trip #1399 remains blocked/unmerged in open PR #1583).
Stage 1 <= 130 lexical words, Stage 2 <= 65 lexical words, zero chatbot openers or word-count postscripts in either stage, and zero files created or modified in the workspace.

lineage_steps: Review all files in `benchmarks/sources/rw4_packaging_264/` (snapshot date 2026-11-25). Fact-check `07-internal-migration-note-draft.md` against the pinned upstream `pypa/packaging` 26.4 sources (`01`–`06`) and return an authoritative 26.4 upgrade contract in at most 130 words correcting every error in the draft and noting any other breaking or license-validation changes in `02`/`05` relevant to migration.

Update: Service A is stuck on Python 3.9 until Q1; Service B runs Python 3.12 and needs both `VersionRange` pickling and guaranteed `Marker` backslash round-trip safety (`#1399`) before upgrading. Write a Slack-ready engineering handoff of at most 65 words stating what 26.4 unblocks vs. what remains blocked for Service A and Service B.
valid_neighbouring_case: When a migration note accurately reflects all upstream changelog entries and cites only merged PRs, the brief confirms upgrade readiness concisely without inventing conflicts.
